main_body: Barn: a large tiled roof slope (rows 6-57) over a red plank front wall with a double X-braced door and two small windows (rows 58-89), on a stone foundation
top_band: Roof slope of red/orange scalloped tiles rows 6-57, with a cream ridge highlight at rows 6-7 and a cream front-edge line at rows 56-57
evidence: Reading down the middle column: ridge cap, then a long tiled roof slope seen from above with a dormer, then a bright cream eave edge at rows 56-57, then a dark shadow row at 58-59 under the eave, then the vertical plank wall with the door. The roof is a large foreshortened surface read the same way as the reference house roofs, and the front wall sits below it. The door and windows have dark inset frames. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The roof tiles carry cream, orange, light red, mid red, dark red and deep maroon, with a per-tile highlight and scallop pattern comparable to the references. The outline is a dark brown/maroon tint, not neutral black. The walls have two-tone vertical plank grain and the foundation has stone speckle. The door's pale frame and the wall are somewhat cleaner and flatter than the references' timber and stone detail, so density is slightly lower, but still acceptable beside them.
